questions.stem: A 49-year-old man has 8 months of bulky, oily, foul-smelling stools that float, and he has lost 7 kg. He has drunk about a liter of vodka a day for 20 years and has had several past episodes of epigastric pain that spread to the back. Results: 72-hour fecal fat 28 g/day (normal < 7 g/day); urinary D-xylose recovered after an oral load within the normal range; serum IgA anti-tissue transglutaminase negative with a normal total IgA; fasting glucose 168 mg/dL. Which is the most likely cause of his steatorrhea?
choices: Celiac disease
Bacterial overgrowth of the small bowel
Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
Whipple disease
Tropical sprue
questions.explanation: Healthy mucosa absorbs **D-xylose** without help from pancreatic enzymes, so a **normal D-xylose test** with steatorrhea means the mucosa works and digestion is the problem. Years of heavy drinking, past pancreatitis-like pain and new hyperglycemia fit **chronic pancreatitis** with loss of lipase. Celiac disease would lower D-xylose absorption and usually make anti-tTG positive. Bacterial overgrowth also lowers D-xylose, because bacteria in the lumen use up the sugar.
questions.explanation_pt: A mucosa saudável absorve a **D-xilose** sem ajuda das enzimas pancreáticas; por isso, um **teste da D-xilose normal** com esteatorreia indica que a mucosa funciona e o problema está na digestão. Anos de consumo excessivo de álcool, dor prévia sugestiva de pancreatite e hiperglicemia recente indicam **pancreatite crônica** com perda de lipase. A doença celíaca reduziria a absorção de D-xilose e geralmente tornaria o anti-tTG positivo. O supercrescimento bacteriano também reduz a D-xilose, porque as bactérias da luz consomem o açúcar.

questions.stem: An 8-year-old girl is short for her age and has had loose stools for 2 years. She has iron deficiency anemia that did not improve with oral iron. She has had pneumonia twice and frequent sinus infections. Serum IgA anti-tissue transglutaminase antibody is negative. Duodenal biopsy shows villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia and many intraepithelial lymphocytes. Her stools and anemia improve on a gluten-free diet. Which additional laboratory finding best explains the negative antibody test?
choices: Very low serum IgA with normal IgG
Absent B cells in the peripheral blood
Absence of HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8
Very high serum IgE
Low CD4+ T-cell count
questions.explanation: The biopsy and the response to a gluten-free diet show **celiac disease**, yet the IgA-based antibody test is negative. **Selective IgA deficiency** is more common in people with celiac disease, and a patient who makes no IgA cannot make **IgA anti-tTG**, so the result is **falsely negative**; her sinus and lung infections also fit IgA deficiency. Absent B cells (X-linked agammaglobulinemia) would remove all antibody classes and cause severe infections from about 6 months of age in boys. Lack of HLA-DQ2 and DQ8 would make celiac disease very unlikely rather than explain a false-negative test.
questions.explanation_pt: A biópsia e a resposta à dieta sem glúten mostram **doença celíaca**, mas o teste de anticorpo baseado em IgA é negativo. A **deficiência seletiva de IgA** é mais comum em pessoas com doença celíaca, e quem não produz IgA não consegue produzir **anti-tTG IgA**, então o resultado é **falsamente negativo**; as infecções sinusais e pulmonares também combinam com deficiência de IgA. A ausência de linfócitos B (agamaglobulinemia ligada ao X) eliminaria todas as classes de anticorpos e causaria infecções graves a partir dos 6 meses de idade, em meninos. A ausência de HLA-DQ2 e DQ8 tornaria a doença celíaca muito improvável, em vez de explicar um teste falsamente negativo.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes has 6 months of bloating, loose stools and fatigue. Hemoglobin is 10.2 g/dL with a low mean corpuscular volume. Serum IgA anti-tissue transglutaminase antibody is strongly positive, and duodenal biopsy shows flattened villi with many intraepithelial lymphocytes. Which event is central to the immune injury in her small bowel?
choices: Wheat proteins cross-linking IgE on mucosal mast cells
Antibodies blocking intrinsic factor from binding vitamin B12
A bacterial toxin raising cAMP in crypt enterocytes
Absence of a brush-border enzyme for a dietary sugar
Deamidated gliadin presented on HLA-DQ2 to CD4+ T cells
questions.explanation: In **celiac disease**, **tissue transglutaminase** deamidates gliadin peptides (glutamine becomes glutamate). The modified peptides bind tightly to **HLA-DQ2** (or DQ8) on antigen-presenting cells and activate **CD4+ T cells**, whose cytokines, together with intraepithelial cytotoxic lymphocytes, destroy the villi. IgE-mediated wheat allergy is a different disease: it causes hives, wheezing or anaphylaxis soon after eating wheat, without villous atrophy. Anti-tTG antibodies are a useful marker, but the T-cell response drives the injury.
questions.explanation_pt: Na **doença celíaca**, a **transglutaminase tecidual** desamida os peptídeos de gliadina (a glutamina vira glutamato). Os peptídeos modificados se ligam fortemente ao **HLA-DQ2** (ou DQ8) das células apresentadoras de antígeno e ativam **linfócitos T CD4+**, cujas citocinas, junto com os linfócitos citotóxicos intraepiteliais, destroem as vilosidades. A alergia ao trigo mediada por IgE é outra doença: causa urticária, sibilância ou anafilaxia logo após ingerir trigo, sem atrofia vilositária. Os anticorpos anti-tTG são um bom marcador, mas a resposta de linfócitos T é que causa a lesão.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman with systemic sclerosis has tight skin on her fingers and Raynaud phenomenon. For 6 months she has had bloating, greasy stools and a 5-kg weight loss. Results: hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 108 fL; serum vitamin B12 low; serum folate high; urinary D-xylose after an oral load low. A glucose breath test shows an early rise in breath hydrogen. She has had no abdominal surgery. Which mechanism best explains her fat malabsorption?
choices: Destruction of pancreatic acini by fibrosis
Bacterial deconjugation of bile acids in the lumen
Gluten-driven T-cell injury of the villi
Failure of bile acid uptake in the terminal ileum
Absent assembly of apoB-48 chylomicrons in enterocytes
questions.explanation: Systemic sclerosis weakens small bowel motility, and the resulting stasis allows **small intestinal bacterial overgrowth**. The bacteria **deconjugate bile acids**, which are then absorbed too early and form micelles poorly, so fat is not absorbed; the bacteria also **consume B12** and **make folate**, giving the pattern of low B12 with high folate. Terminal ileal disease or resection also causes B12 deficiency and bile acid loss, but it would not raise serum folate, and she has had no surgery. Pancreatic insufficiency would leave the D-xylose test normal.
questions.explanation_pt: A esclerose sistêmica enfraquece a motilidade do intestino delgado, e a estase resultante permite o **supercrescimento bacteriano no intestino delgado**. As bactérias **desconjugam os ácidos biliares**, que são absorvidos cedo demais e formam micelas com dificuldade, então a gordura não é absorvida; as bactérias também **consomem B12** e **produzem folato**, o que dá o padrão de B12 baixa com folato alto. Doença ou ressecção do íleo terminal também causa deficiência de B12 e perda de ácidos biliares, mas não elevaria o folato sérico, e ela não fez cirurgia. A insuficiência pancreática deixaria o teste da D-xilose normal.

questions.stem: A 3-year-old boy had rotavirus gastroenteritis with vomiting and watery diarrhea 10 days ago. The vomiting stopped, but he still has watery stools, gas and bloating, mostly after he drinks milk. There is no blood in the stool, and he is well hydrated. Stool studies: sodium 35 mEq/L, potassium 15 mEq/L, osmolality 290 mOsm/kg, pH 5.0, no leukocytes. The diarrhea stops when he does not eat or drink overnight. Which mechanism best explains his ongoing diarrhea?
choices: A toxin keeping CFTR chloride channels open
Inflammatory damage of the colonic mucosa
Loss of bile acid reabsorption in the ileum
Loss of lactase from injured villus tips
Rapid transit from high levels of serotonin
questions.explanation: The stool osmotic gap is 290 − 2 × (35 + 15) = **190 mOsm/kg**, which is high and points to **osmotic diarrhea**; the acidic stool and the end of the diarrhea during fasting support this. **Lactase** sits on the tips of the villi, so mucosal injury from rotavirus causes a **temporary secondary lactase deficiency**, and unabsorbed lactose pulls water into the lumen and is fermented by colonic bacteria. Ongoing toxin-driven secretory diarrhea would have a small osmotic gap and would continue during fasting.
questions.explanation_pt: O gap osmótico fecal é 290 − 2 × (35 + 15) = **190 mOsm/kg**, que é alto e indica **diarreia osmótica**; as fezes ácidas e a parada da diarreia com o jejum reforçam isso. A **lactase** fica no topo das vilosidades, então a lesão da mucosa pelo rotavírus causa uma **deficiência secundária e temporária de lactase**, e a lactose não absorvida atrai água para a luz e é fermentada pelas bactérias do cólon. Uma diarreia secretora contínua por toxina teria gap osmótico baixo e persistiria durante o jejum.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man returns home after 2 years of volunteer work in a rural village in southern India. For 5 months he has had diarrhea, a 6-kg weight loss and a sore, smooth tongue. Hemoglobin is 9.4 g/dL, and mean corpuscular volume is 112 fL; serum vitamin B12 and folate are both low. Serum IgA anti-tissue transglutaminase is negative with a normal total IgA. Three stool exams for ova and parasites and a Giardia antigen test are negative. Biopsies of the duodenum and terminal ileum both show diffuse blunting of the villi with chronic inflammation, no granulomas and no PAS-positive macrophages. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
choices: Celiac disease
Giardiasis
Tropical sprue
Whipple disease
Crohn disease
questions.explanation: Long residence in the tropics, malabsorption and **megaloblastic anemia** with low **folate and B12**, plus villous injury that reaches the **terminal ileum**, fit **tropical sprue**. Celiac disease can look the same under the microscope, but it mainly affects the proximal bowel, is linked to positive anti-tTG, and B12 deficiency is less typical. Giardiasis is the main travel-related mimic, but repeated stool tests and antigen testing are negative; Crohn disease would cause patchy ulcers or granulomas rather than diffuse villous blunting. Tropical sprue responds to **antibiotics plus folate**, not to a gluten-free diet.
questions.explanation_pt: Longa permanência nos trópicos, má absorção e **anemia megaloblástica** com **folato e B12** baixos, além de lesão vilositária que chega ao **íleo terminal**, indicam **espru tropical**. A doença celíaca pode ser igual ao microscópio, mas afeta principalmente o intestino proximal, está ligada a anti-tTG positivo, e a deficiência de B12 é menos típica. A giardíase é o principal diagnóstico diferencial em viajantes, mas os exames de fezes repetidos e o teste de antígeno são negativos; a doença de Crohn causaria úlceras salteadas ou granulomas, e não atrofia vilositária difusa. O espru tropical responde a **antibióticos com folato**, e não à dieta sem glúten.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man has a neuroendocrine tumor of the ileum with many liver metastases. For 2 years he has had episodes of facial flushing and watery diarrhea, and his urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) is very high. Over the last 2 months he has developed a rough, scaly, darkened rash on the back of his hands and the sides of his neck, which are exposed to the sun. His wife says he has become forgetful and irritable. Which mechanism best explains his new findings?
choices: Fat malabsorption causing vitamin A deficiency
Ileal tumor blocking vitamin B12 absorption
Serotonin-driven fibrosis of the skin
Histamine release causing chronic urticaria
Tryptophan used up for serotonin synthesis
questions.explanation: The body makes part of its **niacin (vitamin B3)** from **tryptophan**. A large carcinoid tumor burden turns much of the dietary tryptophan into **serotonin**, so less is left for niacin, and **pellagra** develops: dermatitis in sun-exposed skin, diarrhea and dementia. Vitamin B12 deficiency can cause memory loss, but it causes neuropathy and megaloblastic anemia rather than a photosensitive scaly rash. Serotonin-driven fibrosis affects the right heart valves, not the skin.
questions.explanation_pt: O corpo produz parte da **niacina (vitamina B3)** a partir do **triptofano**. Uma grande massa de tumor carcinoide desvia grande parte do triptofano da dieta para a síntese de **serotonina**; assim, sobra menos para a niacina e surge a **pelagra**: dermatite em áreas expostas ao sol, diarreia e demência. A deficiência de vitamina B12 pode causar perda de memória, mas causa neuropatia e anemia megaloblástica, e não erupção descamativa fotossensível. A fibrose causada pela serotonina atinge as valvas do coração direito, e não a pele.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old woman has had sudden, severe pain around the umbilicus for 4 hours. She has atrial fibrillation and stopped taking her anticoagulant 2 weeks ago. She vomited once and had a loose bowel movement. Pulse is 118/min and irregularly irregular, and blood pressure is 138/84 mm Hg. She is writhing in pain, but the abdomen is soft and only mildly tender, with no guarding. Results: leukocyte count 18,500/mm³; serum lactate 5.2 mmol/L (normal < 2); serum lipase normal. Which artery is most likely blocked?
choices: Superior mesenteric artery
Celiac trunk
Inferior mesenteric artery
Splenic artery
Internal iliac artery
questions.explanation: Sudden pain **out of proportion to the exam**, high lactate and atrial fibrillation without anticoagulation point to **acute mesenteric ischemia** from an embolus. Emboli lodge most often in the **superior mesenteric artery**, which is wide and leaves the aorta at a narrow angle, and periumbilical pain fits the midgut it supplies. The inferior mesenteric artery territory is the usual site of **ischemic colitis**, which causes milder left-sided pain with bloody diarrhea, often after low blood flow. Emboli reach the celiac trunk far less often, and its territory has rich collateral supply.
questions.explanation_pt: Dor súbita **desproporcional ao exame físico**, lactato alto e fibrilação atrial sem anticoagulação indicam **isquemia mesentérica aguda** por êmbolo. Os êmbolos se alojam com mais frequência na **artéria mesentérica superior**, que é larga e sai da aorta em ângulo agudo, e a dor periumbilical combina com o intestino médio que ela irriga. O território da artéria mesentérica inferior é o local habitual da **colite isquêmica**, que causa dor mais leve à esquerda com diarreia sanguinolenta, muitas vezes após baixo fluxo. Os êmbolos chegam ao tronco celíaco com muito menos frequência, e seu território tem rica circulação colateral.
